Liberia Trade-Quick Inc. v. Panama Golden Light Overseas Management S.A. — Dispute over Compensation for Vessel Collision Damage

Plaintiff (Counterclaim Defendant): Liberia Trade-Quick Inc. (TRADE-QUICKER-INC-MONROVIA-LIBERIA)
Address: No. 80, Monrovia, Republic of Liberia.
Representative: Lü Xiaoliang, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Xie Shengxin, Deputy General Manager of Hong Kong Huatong Shipping Agency Co., Ltd.
Agent ad litem: Xu Tanghua, Attorney at Tianjin No. 7 Law Firm.

Defendant (Counterclaim Plaintiff): Panama Golden Light Overseas Management S.A. (GOLDEN-LIGHT-OVERSEAS-MANAGEMENT-S.A-PANAMA)
Address: Osaka, Japan. C/O KOTAIN STEAMSHIP CO., LTD., KOTAIN BUILDING, 18-11, CHOME, EDOBORI, NISHI-KU.
Representative: Kodani Michihiko, President of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Fang Guoqing, Attorney at Tianjin Foreign Economic Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Liberia Trade-Quick Inc. (hereinafter referred to as "Plaintiff"), owner of the M/V TRADE QUICKER, filed an action with the Tianjin Maritime Court against the defendant, Panama Golden Light Overseas Management S.A. (hereinafter referred to as "Defendant"), owner of the M/V YANAN, for compensation for damages arising from a collision between the vessels. The Defendant filed a counterclaim. The Tianjin Maritime Court consolidated the actions in accordance with law.

Plaintiff's Allegations:
The Plaintiff alleged that on July 10, 1989, at 34°36′N (N denotes north latitude, same below), 123°05′E (E denotes east longitude, same below), while the Plaintiff's vessel "Trade Quicker" was en route to Hong Kong at a speed of 9 knots ("knot" denotes nautical speed, 1 knot = 1.852 km/h, same below) on a true course of 178°, when the distance between the two vessels was 1.2 nautical miles, the Defendant's vessel "Yanan," without any sound signal, suddenly turned to port, causing the bow of the "Yanan" to collide with the port quarter of the "Trade Quicker," resulting in the sinking of the "Trade Quicker" and casualties among its crew. The "Yanan" failed to maintain a proper lookout, failed to maintain its course and speed, and suddenly turned to port when approaching the "Trade Quicker," in violation of Rules 5, 7, 8, and 17 of the *International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972*. Accordingly, the Plaintiff sought compensation from the Defendant for economic losses totaling USD 2,917,728.

Defendant's Defense and Counterclaim:
The Defendant argued and counterclaimed that on July 10, 1989, at 1340 hours, while the Defendant's vessel "Yanan" was en route to Kurosaki Port, Japan, at a true course of 103° and a speed of 12.5 knots, at position 34°28′N, 122°32′E, upon first sighting the "Trade Quicker," it maintained its course and speed. At 1408 hours, when the distance between the vessels had reduced to 0.5 nautical miles and it was observed that the "Trade Quicker" had not yet given way, the "Yanan" altered course to 95°. Subsequently, the "Trade Quicker," without any sound signal, suddenly turned sharply to starboard, causing the bow of the "Yanan" to collide with the port side of the "Trade Quicker," resulting in significant damage to the bow of the "Yanan." The "Trade Quicker" seriously neglected its lookout duties, creating a close-quarters situation, and took evasive action too late, in violation of Rules 5, 8, 15, 16, and 34 of the *International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972*. Accordingly, the Plaintiff should bear primary liability for the collision, and the Defendant counterclaimed for compensation of USD 370,000 from the Plaintiff.

Prior to the filing of this action, on December 29, 1989, the Plaintiff applied for preservation of maritime claims. The Tianjin Maritime Court, in accordance with law, ordered the detention of the Defendant's vessel "Yanan." The Defendant, through the Tianjin Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China on behalf of Sumitomo Marine & Fire Insurance Co., Ltd. (Japan), provided a guarantee letter of USD 3,000,000 on January 11, 1990. The Tianjin Maritime Court lifted the detention of the "Yanan" on the following day.

Facts Found by the Court:
Around 1400 hours on July 10, 1989, the sea area through which the two vessels were navigating was overcast, with cloudy skies, southeast winds of force 3–5, light seas, a current of 1.5 knots, and visibility of approximately 10 nautical miles. The current direction was 180°.

The Plaintiff's vessel, "Trade Quicker," was an ocean-going cargo vessel with a length of 79.26 meters, breadth of 12.53 meters, depth of 7.10 meters, main engine of 1,500 HP six-cylinder diesel, gross tonnage of 1,206.4 tons, net tonnage of 659.02 tons, and deadweight tonnage of 2,985 tons. At the time of the incident, it was carrying 2,519.86 tons of cargo, with a forward draft of 5.68 meters, aft draft of 6.30 meters, and mean draft of 5.99 meters. The vessel departed from Tianjin Xingang, China, at 1400 hours on July 8, 1989, bound for Hong Kong. At around 1200 hours on July 10, 1989, its satellite navigation position was 34°46′N, 123°05′E, sailing on a true course of 178° at a speed of approximately 9.5 knots. Between 1341 and 1355 hours on the same day, the officer on watch of the "Trade Quicker" observed the "Yanan" heading east on its starboard side, bearing approximately 80°, at a distance of about 4–6 nautical miles. By 1405 hours, the distance had reduced to about 1 nautical mile, but the "Trade Quicker" still did not take active evasive action. Only at 1407–1408 hours, when the distance had reduced to 0.5–0.6 nautical miles and a close-quarters situation had developed, did it switch from automatic steering to manual steering. Without communicating with the "Yanan," it applied 10° starboard rudder, followed by another 10° to starboard. Approximately one minute after applying starboard rudder, it began to reduce the rudder angle, continuing with only small-angle starboard rudder to avoid collision. No change in speed was made until the collision occurred at about 1410 hours.

The Defendant's vessel, "Yanan," was an ocean-going cargo vessel with a length of 135.06 meters, breadth of 21.83 meters, depth of 11.31 meters, main engine of 8,000 HP six-cylinder diesel, gross tonnage of 8,957.04 tons, net tonnage of 6,322.23 tons. At the time of the incident, it was carrying 11,571 tons of cargo, with a forward draft of 7.35 meters, aft draft of 7.77 meters, and mean draft of approximately 7.46 meters. The vessel departed from Lianyungang, China, at 2300 hours on July 9, 1989, bound for Kurosaki Port, Japan. By around 1200 hours on July 10, 1989, its position was 34°28′N, 122°32′E, sailing on a true course of 103° at a speed of about 12.5 knots. At about 1340 hours, the "Yanan" observed the "Trade Quicker" heading south on its port side, bearing approximately 40°, and continued on its original course and speed. At about 1408 hours, the distance between the vessels had reduced to approximately 0.5 nautical miles, and sensing a risk of collision, intending to pass astern of the "Trade Quicker," the "Yanan" altered its automatic steering course from 103° to 95°. Only when a collision was imminent did it switch to manual steering, applying hard port rudder, stopping engines, and reversing. However, it was too late, and at about 1410 hours, the bow of the "Yanan" collided with the port quarter engine room area of the "Trade Quicker." The collision position was 34°22′N, 123°02′E. The collision caused flooding in the engine room and accommodation of the "Trade Quicker," which rapidly sank by the stern. Except for the Chief Engineer of the "Trade Quicker," Chen Yuechun (CHAN YUI CHUEN), who went down with the vessel, the remaining crew members boarded the "Yanan." The bow, port quarter, and starboard midships of the "Yanan" were damaged. After the crews of both vessels searched the accident area for Chen Yuechun without success, the "Yanan" resumed its original course and proceeded to Kurosaki Port, Japan.

Since both the "Trade Quicker" and the "Yanan" were registered under the flag of Panama, this case should be governed by the laws of the Republic of Panama. The Tianjin Maritime Court notified the parties in writing to provide relevant Panamanian laws, but neither party did so. Unable to ascertain the relevant laws of Panama, and with the consent of both parties, the court decided to apply the law of the forum (*lex fori*) as the governing law. In accordance with Article 117, paragraphs 2 and 3, Article 119, Article 134, paragraph 1, and Article 142, paragraph 3 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China*, as well as the relevant provisions of the Ministry of Communications of the People's Republic of China concerning compensation for vessel collisions, and by referring to international practices for general average compensation, the court ascertained that the losses and expenses recoverable by the Plaintiff were as follows:

(1) Value of the "Trade Quicker" as of July 10, 1989: USD 920,000;
(2) Loss of hire after cessation of operations: USD 62,825.40;
(3) Loss of fuel, stores, etc., at the time of sinking: USD 29,013.59;
(4) Costs for personal injury and death: USD 100,350.58;
(5) Crew wages and repatriation costs: USD 36,624.75;
(6) Compensation paid by the shipowner for personal property losses of crew members: USD 14,532.30;
Total: USD 1,170,196.05.
(7) Interest: USD 223,074.63.

The losses and expenses recoverable by the Defendant were as follows:

(1) Repair costs for the "Yanan": USD 145,168.71;
(2) Survey costs for the "Yanan": USD 1,451.43;
(3) Loss of hire during repairs: USD 67,604.83;
(4) Costs paid by the shipowner for personal injuries: USD 3,869.88;
(5) Agency, communication, and travel costs incurred by the shipowner in handling the incident: USD 4,244.16;
(6) Additional port charges: USD 2,145.91;
Total: USD 224,484.92.
(7) Interest: USD 37,928.73.

The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, relevant documents on economic losses of both parties, court hearing records, and the expert report of the accident investigation panel.

Opinion of the Court:

Before the collision, when the two vessels were in sight of one another and in a crossing situation, the Plaintiff's vessel "Trade Quicker" was the give-way vessel, and the Defendant's vessel "Yanan" was the stand-on vessel. From the time the vessels sighted each other until the collision, the "Trade Quicker" failed to navigate with caution, maintain a proper lookout, or make a sufficient and correct assessment of whether a risk of collision existed, relying solely on visual observation. The "Trade Quicker" should have taken substantial early action to keep out of the way of the "Yanan," but it took evasive action too late, creating a risk of collision. Furthermore, it failed to take action such as stopping or reversing engines, and its evasive action consisted only of small-angle turns. The "Trade Quicker" violated Rules 5, 8(1), 15, 16, and 34(1) of the *International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972*. The Plaintiff shall bear primary liability for the collision.

When the "Yanan" was in a crossing situation with the "Trade Quicker," it should have maintained its course and speed. However, due to a failure to keep a proper lookout, and without ascertaining whether the "Trade Quicker" was giving way or giving any signal of its own intention, the "Yanan" abruptly took port-helm action towards the "Trade Quicker" on its port side, contributing to the collision. Such a blind departure from the Rules was not the most effective emergency action to avoid collision. The "Yanan" violated Rules 5, 7(2), 17, and 34(1) and (4) of the *International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972*. The Defendant shall bear secondary liability for the collision.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 106, paragraph 2 and Article 142, paragraph 3 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China*, and with reference to international practice, the Tianjin Maritime Court on June 29, 1992, rendered the following judgment:

1. The Plaintiff shall bear 60% of the collision liability, assuming economic losses of USD 993,410.60 in this case;
2. The Defendant shall bear 40% of the collision liability, assuming economic losses of USD 662,273.73 in this case;
3. In addition to fully bearing its own economic losses, the Defendant shall pay the Plaintiff an additional USD 399,860.08, which shall be remitted to the Plaintiff in a single payment within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment.

The total court costs in this case amount to USD 15,060.14. The Plaintiff shall bear USD 9,036.08; the Defendant shall bear USD 6,024.06.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, neither the Plaintiff nor the Defendant appealed. Both parties have complied with the judgment.
